FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — Directional Bias in Celebrity Parent-Child Factual Retrieval (design-only; nothing executed, no results claimed)

═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. HYPOTHESIS & OPERATIONALIZATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════

H1 (primary, directional bias): For verified real-world celebrity parent-child pairs, model accuracy is higher when the child's name is given and a parent is requested (C→P) than when the parent's name is given and a child is requested (P→C), on the SAME pairs, under mirrored prompt templates.

Formally: let a_ij = 1 if pair i is answered correctly under condition j. H1: E[a_C→P − a_P→C] > 0 (within-pair difference). Tested with McNemar's exact test on discordant pairs; effect size = difference in accuracies with bootstrap CI.

Alternative explanations the design must discriminate (each gets a dedicated lever in §5):
- A1 Fame asymmetry: children are simply less famous than their famous parents, so P→C fails due to lower entity salience, not retrieval direction. Lever: measured fame covariates + stratified analysis + a matched-fame subset.
- A2 One-to-many cardinality: a child has ≤2 biological parents (a constrained set), while a parent may have many children (open set), making P→C inherently harder. Lever: cardinality stratification + "any child" prompt + a single-famous-child subset.
- A3 Prompt sensitivity: the effect is an artifact of template phrasing/name ordering rather than direction. Lever: ≥2 templates per direction, counterbalanced; check direction×template interaction.
- A4 Data contamination: pairs verbatim in training data inflate both directions unequally (e.g., "child of famous parent" phrasing is more common in text, which predicts C→P advantage — itself part of the mechanism, but must be visible). Lever: report accuracy by fame tier; acknowledge that contamination is plausibly the *mechanism* of H1 rather than a confound to eliminate — the design measures it, not removes it.

Decision rule (pre-registered before any run): accept H1 if (a) McNemar p < .05 with sign in predicted direction on the full sample, AND (b) the direction of the difference remains consistent in every cardinality stratum and in the fame-matched subset (even if individually non-significant). If the difference vanishes or reverses in the fame-matched/single-child strata, conclude the effect is explained by A1/A2 and report that. If the difference flips sign or magnitude >15 pp across templates, flag A3 and report the interaction before any H1 conclusion.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
2. DATASET
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Source: Wikidata (property P40 "child" / P25 "mother" / P22 "father") cross-checked against the English Wikipedia biography page of both parties; each pair must have a citation on at least one Wikipedia page (infobox or body). No facts are asserted here — the actual pairs will be pulled and verified at execution time by a researcher with network access; this design only specifies the procedure.

Inclusion criteria (all must hold):
1. Both persons have an English Wikipedia biography page (notability floor).
2. Relationship is documented on Wikidata with a reference, or stated with citation on Wikipedia.
3. Biological/adopted parent-child relation explicitly stated; adoption allowed but flagged (see adjudication §4).
4. Both individuals are primarily known for their own career (the child must not be famous *only* as "child of X" — otherwise P→C is trivially cued by the parent's fame; flag and stratify instead of exclude).
5. Names are unambiguous: unique stage name, or disambiguated in the prompt by profession+era (disambiguation text is fixed per pair and identical across both directions).
6. Living or recently deceased; event knowledge well within any candidate model's training window (child born before 2010 as soft cutoff).

Exclusion criteria:
- Relations disputed or unsourced in both Wikidata and Wikipedia.
- Pairs where the "parent" is famous solely through the child.
- Step/half relations unless explicitly flagged as a separate stratum (default: exclude step-relations from the primary sample; keep as optional exploratory stratum).
- Twins/multiple celebrity children of one parent: allowed, but the parent contributes only ONE randomly pre-selected child to the primary sample to keep rows independent (remaining children go into a cardinality sub-sample).

CSV schema (one row per pair):
pair_id, child_name_canonical, parent_name_canonical, relation_type (biological|adopted), parent_role_requested (father|mother|any), num_famous_children_of_parent (0/1/2+ as verified from the same source set), child_birth_year, parent_birth_year, fame_child (proxy score), fame_parent (proxy score), fame_tier_child, fame_tier_parent, source_url_wikidata, source_url_wiki_child, source_url_wiki_parent, aliases_child (JSON list), aliases_parent (JSON list), disambiguator (fixed phrase), notes.

Fame proxy (for covariate/stratification, computed at build time): log10 of Wikipedia pageview counts (12-month window) for each person; fame_tier = tertile within the sample. Fame-matched subset: pairs where |fame_child − fame_parent| in pageview logs is below the sample median of |differences|.

Cardinality strata (primary analysis axis): S1 = parent has exactly 1 famous child in sample-eligible set; S2 = 2–3; S3 = 4+.

Target size: 150 pairs (with ~10% pre-registered reserve replacements for verification failures → build 165, freeze 150). This is an ESTIMATE, not a computed power result: under the assumption that ~35% of pairs are discordant and ~65–70% of discordances favor C→P, McNemar's exact test at α=.05 has ≈80% power around n≈90–120 discordant-prone pairs; 150 total pairs makes that discordant count plausible. Plan: a 30-pair pilot (one model) to estimate the empirical discordant rate, then adjust n to hit ≥80% power before scaling; if the pilot shows discordance <20%, increase to 200–250 pairs.

Alias table: built during verification — stage names, married names, transliteration variants, honorifics ("L. Smith", "Smith Jr."). Stored per person; used by the scorer (§4). One canonical form per person; the canonical form is what appears in prompts.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. PROMPTS, CONDITIONS, MODEL SPEC
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Conditions (each pair appears in all four cells):
- C→P templates: T1 "Who is the {father/mother} of {child_canonical}{disambiguator}? Answer with the person's full name."; T2 "Name the parent — {father/mother} — of {child_canonical}{disambiguator}."
- P→C templates: T1' "Name a {son/daughter/child} of {parent_canonical}{disambiguator}. Answer with the person's full name."; T2' "Who is a child of {parent_canonical}{disambiguator}?"

Counterbalancing: for each pair, template assignment and item order are randomized with a fixed seed; the two directions of a pair are separated by ≥50 other items in the presentation order to reduce adjacency priming; order of conditions balanced across the run (half of pairs get C→P first).

Fixed sampling parameters (model-agnostic spec): temperature 0 (greedy) for the primary run; max_tokens 64; single completion per item (no self-consistency in the primary analysis; a secondary replication with T=0.7, 3 samples majority-vote is pre-registered as robustness). System prompt fixed and minimal: "Answer the question. If you do not know, reply exactly: I DON'T KNOW." — identical across directions.

Candidate models (any subset available to the executor; design is model-agnostic): one GPT-4-class API model, one Claude-class API model, one open-weights instruct model (e.g., a Llama/Mixtral-class 70B via local inference). For each model, LOG: exact model ID + version string, snapshot/date, stated knowledge cutoff, sampling params, run date. All models get identical prompts and identical scoring pipeline. Primary analysis per model; cross-model comparison secondary.

Negative controls (included, intermixed, ~15% of items, excluded from H1 statistics): pseudo-pairs that satisfy surface statistics but are not real relations — e.g., asking "Who is the mother of {child}" where the child's parents are not famous, and "Name a child of {parent}" where the named parent has no famous children (parent selected to match fame distribution of real parents). Purpose: detect confabulation rate ("hallucinated name" answers) separately per direction. Scoring: any specific name offered = confabulation (count), "I DON'T KNOW" = correct rejection.

Total query volume per model: 150 pairs × 2 directions × 2 templates = 600, + negative controls ≈ 90, + pilot 30×4 ≈ 120, + robustness replication (T=0.7) 600 → ≈ 1,400 calls per model; ×3 models ≈ 4,200 total. Trivially feasible via API; open-weights model runnable on a single GPU node.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. SCORING & ADJUDICATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Correctness ladder (applied mechanically first, human second):
1. Refusal: exact "I DON'T KNOW" (case-insensitive) → scored REFUSAL (separate from wrong; reported as its own rate per direction).
2. Exact match: normalized answer (lowercase, punctuation/accents stripped) equals canonical name or any alias → CORRECT.
3. Fuzzy match: token-set overlap with canonical/alias names ≥ threshold (e.g., Jaro-Winkler ≥ 0.90 on best-matching full-name pair) → flagged BORDERLINE → human adjudication.
4. Otherwise → INCORRECT; additionally tag INCORRECT-SPECIFIC (a real person's name, wrong relation) vs CONFABULATION (plausible-sounding but non-matching name) vs other.

Primary metric: accuracy = CORRECT / (CORRECT + INCORRECT, i.e., refusals counted as incorrect in the binary score) — pre-registered; refusal rates reported separately per direction so a refusal-driven vs error-driven asymmetry is visible.

Adjudication rules (fixed in advance, adjudicator blind to condition when possible):
- Adoption: if the prompt asks for "father/mother" and the verified relation is adoptive, answer naming the adoptive parent in the correct role counts CORRECT; biological parent counts CORRECT too if the model names the biologically-related famous person, since the relation "parent" is factually true; prompt text avoids asserting biological ties ("parent" wording used in T-variants for adoptive pairs).
- Step-parents/stechildren: excluded from primary sample (§2); if model names a step-relation, scored INCORRECT with an edge-case tag.
- Scenic/stage names: any documented alias in the alias table = CORRECT; a name not in the table but referring to the same person per adjudicator = CORRECT (logged as alias-extension; alias table updated only after the primary scoring pass to avoid post-hoc drift, extensions analyzed as sensitivity check).
- Partial names (e.g., surname only when unambiguous for that person): CORRECT if adjudicator confirms unique reference; ambiguous surname → BORDERLINE → human decision with pre-set tie rule (surname+initial must disambiguate, else INCORRECT).
- Multiple children named when one was asked (P→C): CORRECT if at least one named child is a verified child of the parent and it is the target or any verified famous child (per "any child" phrasing); extra wrong names in the list → BORDERLINE.
- Disagreements: two independent adjudicators for all BORDERLINE cases; Cohen's κ reported; third-party tiebreak.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. ANALYSIS PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Primary test: McNemar's exact test on the 2×2 within-pair table (both correct / only C→P / only P→C / both wrong) per model, on the full frozen sample. Report: discordant counts, exact p, difference in accuracies Δ = acc(C→P) − acc(P→C), and 95% percentile bootstrap CI on Δ (10,000 resamples resampling PAIRS, not items, preserving within-pair dependence).

Stratified analyses (the anti-fame and anti-cardinality levers):
- By cardinality stratum (S1/S2/S3): Δ and within-stratum McNemar. A1/A2 prediction: Δ shrinks toward 0 in S1 (single famous child). H1-as-retrieval-bias prediction: Δ persists in S1.
- Fame-matched subset: same test. Prediction under A1: Δ ≈ 0; under H1: Δ persists.
- Logistic mixed model (secondary): correct ~ direction + template + direction×template + fame_child + fame_parent + num_famous_children + (1|pair), per model — quantifies the direction effect adjusting for covariates.

Pre-registered decision criterion (as in §1): H1 accepted only if primary test significant in predicted direction AND Δ's sign consistent across the cardinality strata and the fame-matched subset; otherwise the result is attributed to the corresponding confound, and the write-up must state which explanation the pattern supports. Negative-control confabulation rates compared per direction (descriptive; if confabulation is asymmetric, reported as part of the mechanism, not silently pooled).

Multiplicity: one primary test per model; stratified tests labeled exploratory. No outcome-driven dataset changes after freeze.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
6. CONTROLS & VALIDITY THREATS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

- One-to-many asymmetry → "any child" phrasing, single-child-per-parent sampling rule, cardinality stratification (S1 subset is the key control).
- Fame asymmetry → measured fame proxies, tertile tiers, fame-matched subset, fame covariates in the mixed model.
- Prompt sensitivity → 2 templates per direction, counterbalancing, direction×template interaction test, fixed system prompt.
- Position/order effects → randomized fixed-seed ordering, ≥50-item separation of a pair's two conditions, order counterbalanced.
- Ground-truth errors → dual-source verification (Wikidata + cited Wikipedia), pre-registered replacement reserve, published source URLs per pair.
- Scoring drift → mechanical scoring first, frozen alias table for primary pass, blinded dual adjudication with κ, alias extensions only in a sensitivity analysis.
- Confabulation/guessing → negative controls (~15%), refusal counted separately, CONFABULATION tagging.
- Contamination → fame-tier reporting (verbatim-famous pairs concentrate in top tier), knowledge-cutoff logging; mechanism-vs-confound framing stated explicitly.
- Model-version drift mid-run → all calls for a model in one session; version string logged; frozen prompt files checksummed.
- Cherry-picking risk → pilot used only for n calibration (pre-declared), never for prompt iteration toward a desired result; prompt set frozen before pilot scoring.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
7. FEASIBILITY (design-only constraints acknowledged)
═══════════════════════════════════════════

- Request volume: ≈1,400 calls per model (§3), ≈4,200 across three models — modest, single-day API cost; open-weights replication needs one GPU pass over ~720 prompts.
- Executable without API: dataset build protocol (Wikidata SPARQL query spec, verification checklist, CSV/alias schema, fame-proxy computation script spec), prompt files, scoring script (normalization + fuzzy matching + adjudication queue), and the full statistical analysis script (McNemar, bootstrap, mixed model) can all be written and dry-run on synthetic placeholder rows locally — without network — so that at execution time only data and API keys are missing.
- What CANNOT be done here and is explicitly deferred: actual pair collection/verification (network), model runs, pilot, any numeric result. This document contains no executed experiment and no claimed outcomes.
- Illustrative CSV row format (PLACEHOLDER ONLY — names are format illustrations, not verified facts, and will be replaced by source-verified entries at build time):
  pair_id=001, child_name_canonical=<child's canonical name>, parent_name_canonical=<parent's canonical name>, relation_type=biological, parent_role_requested=father, num_famous_children_of_parent=1, fame_child=<pageview-log score>, fame_parent=<score>, fame_tier_child=T2, fame_tier_parent=T3, source_url_wikidata=<wikidata entity URL>, aliases_child=["<variant 1>"], disambiguator=", the <profession> born <year>", notes="".

Deliverables at execution time: frozen dataset CSV + alias table, prompt JSONL, raw responses, scored CSV with tags, adjudication log, analysis notebook, pre-registered decision-rule text (§1/§5).

3. PROMPTS, CONDITIONS, MODEL SPEC
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Conditions (each pair appears in all four cells):
- C→P templates: T1 "Who is the {father/mother} of {child_canonical}{disambiguator}? Answer with the person's full name."; T2 "Name the parent — {father/mother} — of {child_canonical}{disambiguator}."

4. SCORING & ADJUDICATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Correctness ladder (applied mechanically first, human second):
1. Refusal: exact "I DON'T KNOW" (case-insensitive) → scored REFUSAL (separate from wrong; reported as its own rate per direction).
2. Exact match: normalized answer (lowercase, punctuation/accents stripped) equals canonical name or any alias → CORRECT.
3. Fuzzy match: token-set overlap with canonical/alias names ≥ threshold (e.g., Jaro-Winkler ≥ 0.90 on best-matching full-name pair) → flagged BORDERLINE → human adjudication.
4. Otherwise → INCORRECT; additionally tag INCORRECT-SPECIFIC (a real person's name, wrong relation) vs CONFABULATION (plausible-sounding but non-matching name) vs other.

Primary metric: accuracy = CORRECT / (CORRECT + INCORRECT, i.e., refusals counted as incorrect in the binary score) — pre-registered; refusal rates reported separately per direction so a refusal-driven vs error-driven asymmetry is visible.

Adjudication rules (fixed in advance, adjudicator blind to condition when possible):
- Adoption: if the prompt asks for "father/mother" and the verified relation is adoptive, answer naming the adoptive parent in the correct role counts CORRECT; biological parent counts CORRECT too if the model names the biologically-related famous person, since the relation "parent" is factually true; prompt text avoids asserting biological ties ("parent" wording used in T-variants for adoptive pairs).
- Step-parents/stechildren: excluded from primary sample (§2); if model names a step-relation, scored INCORRECT with an edge-case tag.
- Scenic/stage names: any documented alias in the alias table = CORRECT; a name not in the table but referring to the same person per adjudicator = CORRECT (logged as alias-extension; alias table updated only after the primary scoring pass to avoid post-hoc drift, extensions analyzed as sensitivity check).
- Partial names (e.g., surname only when unambiguous for that person): CORRECT if adjudicator confirms unique reference; ambiguous surname → BORDERLINE → human decision with pre-set tie rule (surname+initial must disambiguate, else INCORRECT).
- Multiple children named when one was asked (P→C): CORRECT if at least one named child is a verified child of the parent and it is the target or any verified famous child (per "any child" phrasing); extra wrong names in the list → BORDERLINE.
- Disagreements: two independent adjudicators for all BORDERLINE cases; Cohen's κ reported; third-party tiebreak.

5. ANALYSIS PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Primary test: McNemar's exact test on the 2×2 within-pair table (both correct / only C→P / only P→C / both wrong) per model, on the full frozen sample. Report: discordant counts, exact p, difference in accuracies Δ = acc(C→P) − acc(P→C), and 95% percentile bootstrap CI on Δ (10,000 resamples resampling PAIRS, not items, preserving within-pair dependence).

Stratified analyses (the anti-fame and anti-cardinality levers):
- By cardinality stratum (S1/S2/S3): Δ and within-stratum McNemar. A1/A2 prediction: Δ shrinks toward 0 in S1 (single famous child). H1-as-retrieval-bias prediction: Δ persists in S1.
- Fame-matched subset: same test. Prediction under A1: Δ ≈ 0; under H1: Δ persists.
- Logistic mixed model (secondary): correct ~ direction + template + direction×template + fame_child + fame_parent + num_famous_children + (1|pair), per model — quantifies the direction effect adjusting for covariates.

Pre-registered decision criterion (as in §1): H1 accepted only if primary test significant in predicted direction AND Δ's sign consistent across the cardinality strata and the fame-matched subset; otherwise the result is attributed to the corresponding confound, and the write-up must state which explanation the pattern supports. Negative-control confabulation rates compared per direction (descriptive; if confabulation is asymmetric, reported as part of the mechanism, not silently pooled).

Multiplicity: one primary test per model; stratified tests labeled exploratory. No outcome-driven dataset changes after freeze.

6. CONTROLS & VALIDITY THREATS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

- One-to-many asymmetry → "any child" phrasing, single-child-per-parent sampling rule, cardinality stratification (S1 subset is the key control).
- Fame asymmetry → measured fame proxies, tertile tiers, fame-matched subset, fame covariates in the mixed model.
- Prompt sensitivity → 2 templates per direction, counterbalancing, direction×template interaction test, fixed system prompt.
- Position/order effects → randomized fixed-seed ordering, ≥50-item separation of a pair's two conditions, order counterbalanced.
- Ground-truth errors → dual-source verification (Wikidata + cited Wikipedia), pre-registered replacement reserve, published source URLs per pair.
- Scoring drift → mechanical scoring first, frozen alias table for primary pass, blinded dual adjudication with κ, alias extensions only in a sensitivity analysis.
- Confabulation/guessing → negative controls (~15%), refusal counted separately, CONFABULATION tagging.
- Contamination → fame-tier reporting (verbatim-famous pairs concentrate in top tier), knowledge-cutoff logging; mechanism-vs-confound framing stated explicitly.
- Model-version drift mid-run → all calls for a model in one session; version string logged; frozen prompt files checksummed.
- Cherry-picking risk → pilot used only for n calibration (pre-declared), never for prompt iteration toward a desired result; prompt set frozen before pilot scoring.
